Add a fifth terminal state rather than widening either set.
Derive UNVALIDATED_VALIDATION_STATUSES = NON_CLEAN_VALIDATION_STATUSES -
CLI_FAILURE_VALIDATION_STATUSES so no third literal set can drift.
classify_loaded_result returns SubmitTerminalState.unvalidated when there are no
failed queries, no translation fallback, and the validation status falls in that
derived set. `benchbox submit` keeps refusing (exit 1) with an accurate message;
UAT omits `unvalidated` from submit_state_is_cell_failure and reports it as its

description:
benchbox/core/results/status.py defines two sets and documents the correct policy
boundary in a comment: NON_CLEAN_VALIDATION_STATUSES (broad, includes not_run and
not_validated) governs publication, while CLI_FAILURE_VALIDATION_STATUSES
(narrow) governs whether a run FAILED. The comment states plainly that a
completed run whose validation never executed -- DataFrame mode, --validation
disabled -- is not a failed run.

submit_classification.classify_loaded_result ignores that boundary. It calls
result_non_clean_reason (broad set) and collapses every non-clean result that has
no failed queries into SubmitTerminalState.schema_violation.

Two surfaces are wrong as a result:
  - `benchbox submit` refuses DataFrame results with the message 'result is not a
    clean pass', naming a schema violation that did not occur. Refusal is
    correct; the stated reason is not.
  - tests/uat/runner.py::submit_state_is_cell_failure lists schema_violation, so
    UAT downgrades every DataFrame cell to FAILED.

OBSERVED 2026-07-31, release-gate stage 1: six DataFrame platforms reported 0%
pass. True rates once corrected by hand: polars-df 80%, datafusion-df 80%,
pandas-df 69%, pyspark-df 64%, dask-df 55%. Draft at
~/.todo-db/finding-drafts/benchbox/dataframe-schema-violation-misclassification-2026-07-31.md.

anti_patterns.dont: hand-maintain a third literal status set
anti_patterns.instead: derive it by set subtraction and assert the partition in a test
anti_patterns.why: the two existing sets already drifted in effect; a third invites the same failure

anti_patterns.dont: make UAT treat unvalidated as a plain pass with no separate reporting
anti_patterns.instead: pass the cell but report unvalidated in its own column in matrix_summary.tsv
anti_patterns.why: it would hide the fact that a majority of DataFrame cells are unverified, replacing a false alarm with false confidence

anti_patterns.instead: add a distinct terminal state and leave both sets intact
anti_patterns.why: that set governs publication -- dropping them would let genuinely unvalidated results be published as clean, which is far worse than the reporting bug being fixed

anti_patterns.dont: special-case DataFrame platforms by name anywhere in the classifier
anti_patterns.instead: classify on validation status, which is the actual signal
anti_patterns.why: the classifier is shared with `benchbox submit`, where platform identity is not a legitimate input; --validation-disabled SQL runs hit the same path

preserves.behavior: NON_CLEAN_VALIDATION_STATUSES and CLI_FAILURE_VALIDATION_STATUSES keep their current membership.
`benchbox submit` still refuses an unvalidated result with a non-zero exit; only the message changes. Publication policy is NOT loosened.
compliance_class refusal is still checked BEFORE clean-ness, so an unofficial-and-unvalidated result still classifies as unofficial.
query_failure, schema_violation and missing_manifest keep their existing meanings and stay UAT cell failures.

prior_art.concept: CLI_FAILURE_VALIDATION_STATUSES and its comment already encode the exact policy boundary this item applies; derive from it rather than adding a third literal set
single-source-of-truth classifier shared by CLI and UAT specifically so the two cannot drift; the new state must be added here, not at either call site
existing contract test asserts CLI and UAT agree per state; extend its case table with the new state
